Anatomy-02: Embryology.question: ১) What is the duration of embryonic period?
Anatomy-02: Embryology.exp:
The embryonic period extends from the beginning of the 3rd week to the end of the 8th week of development after fertilization. This is the critical period of organogenesis, during which the major organs and body systems are formed. Consequently, the embryo is most susceptible to teratogens during this stage, and exposure to harmful agents may result in major congenital anomalies.

The 2nd week is part of the pre-embryonic (germinal) period, while the fetal period begins at the 9th week and continues until birth.

Anatomy-02: Embryology.question: ২) Which is not a stage of embryogenesis?
Anatomy-02: Embryology.exp:
Embryogenesis is the process of development of the embryo after fertilization. It includes sequential stages such as cleavage, gastrulation, neurulation, and organogenesis. These processes transform the zygote into a multicellular embryo with differentiated tissues and organs.

Fertilization is the event that precedes embryogenesis. It involves the fusion of the sperm and ovum to form the zygote, thereby initiating embryonic development, but it is not itself a stage of embryogenesis.

Anatomy-02: Embryology.question: ৩) What is the time of onset of Oogenesis?
Anatomy-02: Embryology.exp:
Oogenesis begins during intrauterine (fetal) life. Primordial germ cells migrate to the developing ovary and differentiate into oogonia, which proliferate by mitosis. The oogonia then become primary oocytes that enter meiosis I and arrest in prophase I (dictyotene stage) until puberty.

At puberty, a few primary oocytes resume meiosis during each menstrual cycle. Meiosis II is completed only if fertilization occurs.

Anatomy-02: Embryology.question: ৪) How long the Ovum remain viable after discharge?
Anatomy-02: Embryology.exp:
After ovulation, the secondary oocyte (ovum) remains viable for approximately 24 hours. During this period, it can be fertilized by a sperm. If fertilization does not occur within 24 hours, the ovum degenerates and loses its capacity for fertilization.

In contrast, sperm can remain viable in the female reproductive tract for approximately 3–5 days, allowing fertilization to occur even if intercourse takes place several days before ovulation.

Anatomy-02: Embryology.question: ৫) What is the site of storage for sperm?
Anatomy-02: Embryology.exp:
The epididymis, particularly its tail (cauda epididymis), is the principal site for storage and maturation of sperm. During their passage through the epididymis, sperm acquire motility and the ability to fertilize an ovum.

The other options are incorrect:

  • Testis – Site of spermatogenesis, not sperm storage.

  • Seminal vesicle – Produces a fructose-rich seminal fluid but does not store sperm.

  • Vas deferens – Transports sperm from the epididymis during ejaculation and has only a limited storage role.

Anatomy-02: Embryology.question: ৬) How long corpus luteum acts as temporary endocrine gland?
Anatomy-02: Embryology.exp:
After fertilization, the corpus luteum of pregnancy is maintained by human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) secreted by the trophoblast. It functions as a temporary endocrine gland, producing progesterone (and smaller amounts of estrogen) to maintain the endometrium and support early pregnancy.

By the end of the first trimester (about 10–12 weeks, approximately 3 months), the placenta becomes the primary source of progesterone and estrogen, and the corpus luteum gradually regresses.

Anatomy-02: Embryology.question: ৭) All of the following are content of menstrual blood except--?
Anatomy-02: Embryology.exp:
Normal menstrual blood does not clot because it contains fibrinolysin, an enzyme released from the endometrium that dissolves fibrin and prevents clot formation. Menstrual fluid is a mixture of blood, shed endometrial tissue (including uterine gland fragments), cervical mucus, vaginal secretions, and, if ovulation has occurred, an unfertilized ovum.

Although large clots may occasionally be seen in women with heavy menstrual bleeding, clotted blood is not a normal component of menstrual blood.

Anatomy-02: Embryology.question: ৮) The outer cell mass of blastocyst forms---?
Anatomy-02: Embryology.exp:
The outer cell mass of the blastocyst is called the trophoblast. It gives rise to the chorion and forms the fetal part of the placenta. The trophoblast also differentiates into the cytotrophoblast and syncytiotrophoblast, which are essential for implantation and placental development.

The other options are incorrect:

  • Embryo develops from the inner cell mass (embryoblast).

  • Primitive streak arises from the epiblast during gastrulation.

  • Hypoblast is also derived from the inner cell mass.

Anatomy-02: Embryology.question: ৯) The process of formation of three germ layers in embryo is called--?
Anatomy-02: Embryology.exp:
Gastrulation is the process by which the three primary germ layers—ectoderm, mesoderm, and endoderm—are formed from the bilaminar embryonic disc. It begins during the 3rd week of embryonic development with the formation of the primitive streak. These three germ layers subsequently give rise to all tissues and organs of the body.

The other options are incorrect:

  • Organogenesis – Formation of organs from the germ layers.

  • Embryogenesis – The overall process of embryonic development.

  • Cleavage – Rapid mitotic divisions of the zygote producing blastomeres without an increase in overall size.

Anatomy-02: Embryology.question: ১০) Which gland does not arise from surface ectoderm?
Anatomy-02: Embryology.exp:
The adrenal cortex is derived from the mesoderm (coelomic epithelium) and therefore does not arise from the surface ectoderm.

The other glands are derived from surface ectoderm:

  • Hypophysis cerebri (anterior pituitary/adenohypophysis) develops from Rathke's pouch, an ectodermal outgrowth from the roof of the primitive mouth (surface ectoderm). (The posterior pituitary is derived from neuroectoderm.)

  • Mammary gland is a modified surface ectodermal sweat gland.

  • Lacrimal gland develops from surface ectoderm.

Anatomy-02: Embryology.question: ১১) Melanocytes are derived from which of the following germ layer?
Anatomy-02: Embryology.exp:
Melanocytes are derived from the neural crest, a transient population of cells originating from the neuroectoderm. During embryonic development, neural crest cells migrate into the skin and differentiate into melanocytes, which produce the pigment melanin.

The other options are incorrect:

  • Surface ectoderm forms the epidermis, but not melanocytes.

  • Neural tube gives rise to the brain, spinal cord, retina, and posterior pituitary.

  • Paraxial mesoderm forms somites, which develop into skeletal muscle, vertebrae, and dermis.

Anatomy-02: Embryology.question: ১২) Which period is highly sensitive to teratogen?
Anatomy-02: Embryology.exp:
The embryonic period (3rd–8th week after fertilization) is the most sensitive period to teratogens because organogenesis occurs during this time. Exposure to drugs, infections, radiation, or other teratogenic agents can result in major structural congenital malformations.

The other periods are less susceptible:

  • Pre-embryonic period (0–2 weeks): Follows the "all-or-none" phenomenon—exposure either causes embryonic death or has no lasting effect.

  • Fetal period (9 weeks to birth): Teratogens mainly cause growth restriction and functional abnormalities, rather than major structural defects.

  • Early childhood: Not part of prenatal development.

Anatomy-02: Embryology.question: ১৩) Which of the following is adult derivative of notochord?
Anatomy-02: Embryology.exp:
The notochord is a midline embryonic structure that serves as the primary axial support and induces the development of the neural tube. During development, most of the notochord degenerates, but a portion persists in the adult as the nucleus pulposus of the intervertebral disc.

The other options are derived from mesoderm:

  • Annulus fibrosus – Derived from the sclerotome of somites (mesoderm).

  • Vertebra – Develops from the sclerotome.

  • Vertebral canal – Formed by the vertebral arches surrounding the spinal cord.

Anatomy-02: Embryology.question: ১৪) If LMP is 15.4.2018, what will be possible EDD?
Anatomy-02: Embryology.exp:
The Expected Date of Delivery (EDD) is calculated using Naegele's rule:

EDD = LMP + 1 year − 3 months + 7 days
(or LMP + 9 months + 7 days)

LMP: 15.04.2018

  • Add 9 months → 15.01.2019

  • Add 7 days → 22.01.2019

Anatomy-02: Embryology.question: ১৫) Spermiogenesis is the ___ ?
Anatomy-02: Embryology.option4: combined process of formation of sperm and ovum
Anatomy-02: Embryology.exp:
Spermiogenesis is the final stage of spermatogenesis, during which haploid spermatids differentiate into mature spermatozoa without undergoing further cell division. This process involves:

  • Formation of the acrosome

  • Condensation and elongation of the nucleus

  • Development of the flagellum (tail)

  • Arrangement of mitochondria in the middle piece

  • Loss of excess cytoplasm

The other options are incorrect:

  • Process of formation of sperm refers to spermatogenesis.

  • Differentiation of spermatogonia to spermatozoa describes the entire process of spermatogenesis, not spermiogenesis.

  • Combined process of formation of sperm and ovum refers to gametogenesis.

Anatomy-02: Embryology.question: ১৬) What is the normal site of implantation?
Anatomy-02: Embryology.option2: posterior wall of uterus near fundus
Anatomy-02: Embryology.option3: middle of the fundus of uterus
Anatomy-02: Embryology.exp:
The normal site of implantation is the upper part of the uterine cavity, most commonly on the posterior wall near the fundus (less commonly on the anterior wall near the fundus). Implantation usually occurs 6–7 days after fertilization when the blastocyst attaches to the receptive endometrium.

The other options are incorrect:

  • Ampulla of the fallopian tube – This is the usual site of fertilization, not implantation. Implantation here results in a tubal ectopic pregnancy.

  • Middle of the fundus of the uterus – Implantation is typically near the fundus rather than exactly in its middle.

  • Round ligament – Has no role in implantation.

Anatomy-02: Embryology.question: ১৭) Diploid number of chromosome is restored by which process ?
Anatomy-02: Embryology.exp:
Fertilization is the process in which a haploid sperm (23 chromosomes) fuses with a haploid ovum (23 chromosomes) to form a diploid zygote (46 chromosomes). Thus, the diploid chromosome number is restored at fertilization.

The other options are incorrect:

  • Ovulation – Release of the secondary oocyte from the ovary.

  • Spermatogenesis – Produces haploid spermatozoa by meiosis.

  • Implantation – Attachment of the blastocyst to the endometrium and does not affect chromosome number.

Anatomy-02: Embryology.question: ১৮) What is the required time for the total process of spermatogenesis?
Anatomy-02: Embryology.exp:
Spermatogenesis is the process by which spermatogonia develop into mature spermatozoa within the seminiferous tubules of the testes. The entire process takes approximately 74 days, followed by an additional 10–14 days for sperm maturation and storage in the epididymis.

The stages of spermatogenesis include:

  • Mitotic proliferation of spermatogonia

  • Meiosis I and II to form haploid spermatids

  • Spermiogenesis, in which spermatids differentiate into mature spermatozoa

Anatomy-02: Embryology.question: ১৯) Which hormone influences ovulation process?
Anatomy-02: Embryology.exp:
Ovulation is triggered by the mid-cycle surge of luteinizing hormone (LH), which occurs approximately 36 hours before ovulation. The LH surge causes:

  • Rupture of the mature Graafian follicle

  • Release of the secondary oocyte (ovum)

  • Formation of the corpus luteum

The other options are incorrect:

  • FSH stimulates follicular growth and maturation.

  • GnRH from the hypothalamus stimulates the release of LH and FSH from the anterior pituitary but does not directly trigger ovulation.

  • hCG maintains the corpus luteum during early pregnancy and has LH-like activity but is not responsible for normal ovulation.

Anatomy-02: Embryology.question: ২০) Menstrual blood contains which of the following ?
Anatomy-02: Embryology.exp:
At the time of ovulation, the cell released from the ovary is a secondary oocyte, which is arrested in metaphase II of meiosis. If fertilization does not occur, the secondary oocyte degenerates and is shed along with the endometrial tissue during menstruation.

The other options are incorrect:

  • Mature ovum – A true ovum is formed only after fertilization, when the secondary oocyte completes meiosis II.

  • Immature ovum – Not a standard embryological term.

  • Primary oocyte – Remains within the ovarian follicles and is not shed in menstrual blood.

Anatomy-02: Embryology.question: ২১) What is the average duration of menstrual cycle?
Anatomy-02: Embryology.exp:
The average duration of a normal menstrual cycle is 28 days, counted from the first day of one menstrual period to the first day of the next. Ovulation typically occurs around day 14 in a 28-day cycle.

The menstrual cycle consists of:

  • Menstrual phase: Days 1–5

  • Proliferative (follicular) phase: Days 6–14

  • Secretory (luteal) phase: Days 15–28

Although the normal cycle length ranges from 21–35 days in adult women, the average and classically tested duration is 28 days.

Anatomy-02: Embryology.question: ২২) Partial absence of one or more of the extremities is called ____?
Anatomy-02: Embryology.exp:
Meromelia is a congenital anomaly characterized by the partial absence of one or more limbs (extremities) due to defective limb development during embryogenesis.

The other options are incorrect:

  • Amelia – Complete absence of one or more limbs.

  • Phocomelia – Hands or feet are attached close to the trunk because the proximal portions of the limb are absent or severely underdeveloped ("seal limb").

  • Micromelia – All or part of a limb is abnormally small, but not absent.

Anatomy-02: Embryology.question: ২৩) What is the type of human placenta?
Anatomy-02: Embryology.exp:
The human placenta is of the hemochorial type, in which maternal blood comes into direct contact with the chorionic villi. The trophoblast separates the fetal blood from the maternal blood, allowing efficient exchange of gases, nutrients, and waste products without direct mixing of the two circulations.

The other options are incorrect:

  • Heterochorial – Not a recognized classification of the placenta.

  • Hemodecidual – Not a standard placental type.

  • Choriodecidual – Refers to the fetal-maternal interface but is not a classification of placental type.

Anatomy-02: Embryology.question: ২৪) Lateral curving of the spine is called ___?
Anatomy-02: Embryology.exp:
Scoliosis is an abnormal lateral (side-to-side) curvature of the vertebral column, often accompanied by rotation of the vertebrae. It may be congenital, idiopathic, or secondary to neuromuscular disorders.

The other options are incorrect:

  • Kyphosis – Excessive posterior curvature of the thoracic spine ("hunchback").

  • Lordosis – Excessive anterior curvature of the lumbar spine ("swayback").

  • Kyphoscoliosis – Combination of kyphosis and scoliosis.

Anatomy-02: Embryology.question: ২৫) Ligamentum teres hepatis is the remnants of ____?
Anatomy-02: Embryology.exp:
The ligamentum teres hepatis (round ligament of the liver) is the fibrous remnant of the left umbilical vein. During fetal life, the left umbilical vein carries oxygenated blood from the placenta to the fetus. After birth, it becomes obliterated and forms the ligamentum teres hepatis, which lies within the free margin of the falciform ligament.

The other options are incorrect:

  • Right umbilical vein – Normally disappears early in embryonic life.

  • Right and left umbilical arteries – After birth, their distal parts become the medial umbilical ligaments, not the ligamentum teres hepatis.

Anatomy-02: Embryology.question: ২৬) Otic placode gives rise to which of the following ?
Anatomy-02: Embryology.exp:
The otic placode is a thickening of the surface ectoderm that invaginates to form the otic vesicle (otocyst). The otic vesicle gives rise to the membranous labyrinth of the inner ear, including the:

  • Cochlea

  • Utricle

  • Saccule

  • Semicircular ducts

The other options are incorrect:

  • Lens of the eye – Develops from the lens placode.

  • Oral epithelium – Develops from the stomodeal (surface) ectoderm.

  • Nasal epithelium – Develops from the nasal placodes.

Anatomy-02: Embryology.question: ২৭) Anencephaly is caused by failure of fusion of ____?
Anatomy-02: Embryology.exp:
Anencephaly is a severe neural tube defect caused by failure of closure of the anterior (rostral/cranial) neuropore, which normally closes around the 25th day of embryonic development. This results in absence of a major portion of the brain, skull, and scalp, and the condition is incompatible with long-term survival.

The other options are incorrect:

  • Posterior neuropore – Failure of closure causes spina bifida.

  • Lateral neuropore and central neuropore – These are not recognized embryological structures.

Anatomy-02: Embryology.question: ২৮) What is the basis of axial skeleton?
Anatomy-02: Embryology.exp:
The notochord is the primary axial supporting structure of the embryo and serves as the basis for the development of the axial skeleton. It induces the formation of the neural tube and guides the development of the vertebral column. In adults, the only remnant of the notochord is the nucleus pulposus of the intervertebral disc.

The other options are incorrect:

  • Amnion – Forms the amniotic sac surrounding the embryo.

  • Chorion – Contributes to the fetal part of the placenta.

  • Allantois – Contributes to the urachus (median umbilical ligament) and early blood vessel formation.

Anatomy-02: Embryology.question: ২৯) Sex of the embryo is determined at the time of ___?
Anatomy-02: Embryology.exp:
The genetic sex of the embryo is determined at fertilization, when a 23,X ovum is fertilized by either:

  • a 23,X sperm → 46,XX (female), or

  • a 23,Y sperm → 46,XY (male).

Thus, the sperm determines the sex of the embryo by contributing either an X or Y chromosome.

The other options are incorrect:

  • Conception is often used synonymously with fertilization, but fertilization is the precise embryological term.

  • Implantation occurs about 6–7 days after fertilization and does not determine sex.

  • Organogenesis occurs during weeks 3–8 and is unrelated to sex determination.

Anatomy-02: Embryology.question: ৩০) The permanent cessation of menstruation is called ___?
Anatomy-02: Embryology.exp:
Menopause is the permanent cessation of menstruation resulting from the loss of ovarian follicular activity. It is diagnosed retrospectively after 12 consecutive months of amenorrhea in the absence of other pathological or physiological causes. The average age of natural menopause is about 50–51 years.

The other options are incorrect:

  • Menarche – The first menstrual period.

  • Climacteric – The transition period from the reproductive to the non-reproductive phase, encompassing the years before, during, and after menopause.

  • Andropause – Refers to the age-related decline in male gonadal function, not menstruation.

Anatomy-02: Embryology.question: ৩১) Which is not produced during spermatogenesis?
Anatomy-02: Embryology.exp:
Polar bodies are formed only during oogenesis, not during spermatogenesis. They are small haploid cells produced by the unequal meiotic divisions of the primary and secondary oocyte and usually degenerate.

The other options are produced during spermatogenesis:

  • Primary spermatocyte – Formed from spermatogonia before meiosis I.

  • Spermatid – Produced after meiosis II.

  • Spermatozoa – Mature sperm cells formed from spermatids by spermiogenesis.

Anatomy-02: Embryology.question: ৩২) Muscles of the face are derived from which pharyngeal arch?
Anatomy-02: Embryology.exp:
The muscles of facial expression are derived from the 2nd pharyngeal (hyoid) arch and are supplied by the facial nerve (cranial nerve VII).

Derivatives of the 2nd pharyngeal arch include:

  • Muscles of facial expression

  • Stapedius

  • Stylohyoid

  • Posterior belly of the digastric

  • Facial nerve (CN VII)

The other arches give rise to different structures:

  • 1st arch – Muscles of mastication (CN V3)

  • 3rd arch – Stylopharyngeus (CN IX)

  • 4th arch – Pharyngeal constrictors, cricothyroid, levator veli palatini (CN X)

Anatomy-02: Embryology.question: ৩৩) Septum transversum plays important role in the development of ___?
Anatomy-02: Embryology.exp:
The septum transversum is a thick plate of mesoderm that forms the central tendon of the diaphragm. It is one of the four embryological components that contribute to the development of the diaphragm:

  • Septum transversum → Central tendon

  • Pleuroperitoneal membranes

  • Dorsal mesentery of the esophagus → Crura of the diaphragm

  • Muscular ingrowth from the lateral body wall

The other options are incorrect:

  • Pleura – Derived from the intraembryonic mesoderm.

  • Peritoneum – Derived from the lateral plate mesoderm.

  • Pelvic diaphragm – Develops from mesoderm of the pelvic region, not the septum transversum.

Anatomy-02: Embryology.question: ৩৪) Coronary sinus is formed from----?
Anatomy-02: Embryology.exp:
The coronary sinus develops from the left horn of the sinus venosus. During cardiac development:

  • The right horn of the sinus venosus becomes incorporated into the smooth part of the right atrium (sinus venarum).

  • The left horn of the sinus venosus forms the coronary sinus and the oblique vein of the left atrium (vein of Marshall).

The other options are incorrect:

  • Truncus arteriosus → Ascending aorta and pulmonary trunk.

  • Bulbus cordis → Parts of the ventricles, including the smooth outflow tract of the right ventricle.

  • Conus arteriosus → Smooth outflow tract (infundibulum) of the right ventricle.

Anatomy-02: Embryology.question: ৩৫) the lining epithelium of respiratory passage originates from----?
Anatomy-02: Embryology.exp:
The lining epithelium of the respiratory tract (larynx, trachea, bronchi, and lungs) develops from the endoderm of the laryngotracheal diverticulum (respiratory diverticulum), which arises from the ventral wall of the primitive foregut during the 4th week of development.

The supporting structures are derived from mesoderm:

  • Cartilage, connective tissue, smooth muscle, and blood vessels → Splanchnic (visceral) mesoderm

The other options are incorrect:

  • Ectoderm – Forms the epidermis and nervous system.

  • Mesoderm – Forms connective tissue and muscle, not the respiratory epithelium.

  • Ectoendoderm – Not a recognized embryological germ layer.

Anatomy-02: Embryology.question: ৩৬) which is not a derivatives of midgut?
Anatomy-02: Embryology.exp:
The midgut extends from the distal part of the duodenum to the proximal two-thirds of the transverse colon. Its derivatives include:

  • Distal duodenum

  • Jejunum

  • Ileum

  • Cecum

  • Appendix

  • Ascending colon

  • Proximal two-thirds of the transverse colon

The descending colon is a derivative of the hindgut, which also gives rise to:

  • Distal one-third of the transverse colon

  • Descending colon

  • Sigmoid colon

  • Rectum

  • Upper anal canal

Anatomy-02: Embryology.question: ৩৭) Meckel’s diverticulum is a developmental anomaly of which part of gut?
Anatomy-02: Embryology.exp:
Meckel's diverticulum is a congenital anomaly resulting from persistence of the vitelline (omphalomesenteric) duct. It arises from the antimesenteric border of the ileum, usually about 60 cm (2 feet) proximal to the ileocecal valve in adults.

It is therefore an anomaly of the small intestine and is classically remembered by the Rule of 2s:

  • 2% of the population

  • 2 inches long

  • 2 feet from the ileocecal valve

  • May contain 2 types of ectopic mucosa (gastric and pancreatic)

  • Often presents before 2 years of age

Anatomy-02: Embryology.question: ৩৮) which one develops in thoraco-lumber region?
Anatomy-02: Embryology.exp:
The mesonephros develops in the thoracolumbar region of the embryo during the 4th week and functions as a temporary kidney until the permanent kidneys develop.

The other options are incorrect:

  • Pronephros – Develops in the cervical region and is nonfunctional in humans.

  • Metanephros – The permanent kidney, which develops in the sacral (pelvic) region and later ascends to the lumbar region.

  • Ureteric bud – An outgrowth from the mesonephric (Wolffian) duct near the cloaca that forms the collecting system of the kidney; it is not specific to the thoracolumbar region.

Anatomy-02: Embryology.question: ৩৯) Horseshoe shaped kidney appears as a developmental failure of fusion of which pole of kidney?
Anatomy-02: Embryology.exp:
A horseshoe kidney results from fusion of the inferior poles of the two metanephric kidneys during embryonic development. As the fused kidney ascends from the pelvis, its ascent is arrested by the inferior mesenteric artery, so it remains lower than normal in the abdomen.

The other options are incorrect:

  • Superior poles – Rarely fuse.

  • Medial and lateral poles – These are not involved in the typical embryological fusion leading to a horseshoe kidney.

Anatomy-02: Embryology.question: ৪০) All are derivatives of ureteric bud except...?
Anatomy-02: Embryology.exp:
The ureteric bud arises from the mesonephric (Wolffian) duct and gives rise to the collecting system of the kidney, including:

  • Ureter

  • Renal pelvis

  • Major and minor calyces

  • Collecting ducts and collecting tubules

The urethra is not derived from the ureteric bud. It develops mainly from the endoderm of the urogenital sinus (with the distal part of the male urethra developing from ectoderm).

Anatomy-02: Embryology.question: ৪১) what is sometimes called third testis?
Anatomy-02: Embryology.exp:
The epididymis is sometimes referred to as the "third testis" because it is a closely applied, highly coiled duct lying on the posterior aspect of the testis. It is the site where sperm:

  • Mature

  • Gain motility

  • Are stored before ejaculation

The other options are incorrect:

  • Urethra – Conducts urine and semen to the exterior.

  • Prostate – Produces prostatic fluid.

  • Seminal vesicle – Produces fructose-rich seminal fluid.

Anatomy-02: Embryology.question: ৪২) palatine tonsil develops from which pharyngeal pouch?
Anatomy-02: Embryology.exp:
The palatine tonsil develops from the endoderm of the 2nd pharyngeal pouch. The endoderm proliferates to form the tonsillar crypts, while the surrounding lymphoid tissue is derived from infiltrating mesenchymal lymphocytes.

High-yield derivatives of the pharyngeal pouches:

  • 1st pouch → Tympanic cavity and auditory (Eustachian) tube

  • 2nd pouch → Palatine tonsil

  • 3rd pouch → Inferior parathyroid glands and thymus

  • 4th pouch → Superior parathyroid glands and ultimobranchial body (parafollicular C cells of the thyroid)

Anatomy-02: Embryology.question: ৪৩) which one is not developed from 4th pharyngeal arch?
Anatomy-02: Embryology.exp:
The 4th pharyngeal arch gives rise to structures including:

  • Cricothyroid muscle

  • Pharyngeal constrictor muscles

  • Levator veli palatini

  • Superior laryngeal nerve (branch of the vagus nerve, CN X)

  • Contributes to the laryngeal cartilages, including part of the thyroid cartilage

The thymus is not derived from the 4th pharyngeal arch. It develops from the endoderm of the 3rd pharyngeal pouch, along with the inferior parathyroid glands.

Anatomy-02: Embryology.question: ৪৪) Absence of nipple is called---?
Anatomy-02: Embryology.exp:
Athelia is the congenital absence of the nipple, which may occur alone or be associated with other developmental anomalies.

The other options are incorrect:

  • Amelia – Complete absence of one or more limbs.

  • Amastia – Congenital absence of the breast (mammary gland), usually including the nipple and areola.

  • Nomelia – Not a recognized embryological term.

Anatomy-02: Embryology.question: ৪৫) genital tubercle in females gives rise to which of the following?
Anatomy-02: Embryology.exp:
The genital tubercle is the embryonic primordium that develops into the clitoris in females and the penis in males.

The other options are derived from different embryonic structures:

  • Labia majora – Develop from the labioscrotal swellings.

  • Labia minora – Develop from the urogenital (urethral) folds.

  • Vagina – Upper part develops from the paramesonephric (Müllerian) ducts, while the lower part develops from the sinovaginal bulbs of the urogenital sinus.

Anatomy-02: Embryology.question: ৪৬) How many polar bodies are generated during spermatogenesis?
Anatomy-02: Embryology.exp:
Polar bodies are not formed during spermatogenesis. Instead, each primary spermatocyte undergoes meiosis to produce four equal-sized haploid spermatids, which subsequently differentiate into four spermatozoa through spermiogenesis.

In contrast, polar bodies are produced only during oogenesis because meiotic divisions are unequal, allowing one large ovum to retain almost all of the cytoplasm while the small polar bodies usually degenerate.

Anatomy-02: Embryology.question: ৪৭) what types of cell division occurs during cleavage?
Anatomy-02: Embryology.exp:
Cleavage is a series of rapid mitotic cell divisions that occur after fertilization. These divisions increase the number of blastomeres without increasing the overall size of the embryo because the zygote remains enclosed within the zona pellucida.

The other options are incorrect:

  • Amitosis – A direct type of cell division that does not occur during normal human embryogenesis.

  • Meiosis – Occurs only during gametogenesis to produce haploid gametes.

  • No division occurs – Incorrect, as cleavage consists of repeated cell divisions.

Anatomy-02: Embryology.question: ৪৮) what is the colour of corpus albicans?
Anatomy-02: Embryology.exp:
The corpus albicans is a white fibrous scar formed by degeneration of the corpus luteum when pregnancy does not occur. It is composed mainly of dense connective tissue and gradually becomes smaller over time.

The other options are incorrect:

  • Red – Not a characteristic of the corpus albicans.

  • Yellow – Refers to the corpus luteum, which is yellow due to its lipid-rich lutein cells.

  • Green – Has no association with ovarian structures.

Anatomy-02: Embryology.question: ৪৯) which of the following is not formed from urogenital sinus?
Anatomy-02: Embryology.exp:
The urogenital sinus (derived from the endoderm of the cloaca) gives rise to several structures of the lower urinary and genital tracts, including:

  • Bartholin's (greater vestibular) glands

  • Urethral glands (glands of Littre)

  • Paraurethral (Skene's) glands

  • Urinary bladder (except the trigone) and much of the urethra

The seminal vesicle is not derived from the urogenital sinus. It develops as a lateral outgrowth of the mesonephric (Wolffian) duct.

Anatomy-02: Embryology.question: ৫০) deficiency in which of the following causes neural tube defects?
Anatomy-02: Embryology.exp:
Folic acid (vitamin B9) deficiency during early pregnancy is the most important nutritional cause of neural tube defects (NTDs), such as:

  • Anencephaly

  • Spina bifida

  • Encephalocele

Neural tube closure occurs during the 3rd–4th week of embryonic development (days 22–28), often before a woman realizes she is pregnant. Therefore, women planning pregnancy are advised to take 400 μg (0.4 mg) of folic acid daily, beginning before conception and continuing through the first trimester.

The other options are incorrect:

  • Iron – Deficiency causes anemia, not NTDs.

  • Vitamin B12 – Deficiency may contribute to NTD risk but is not the primary cause in standard embryology questions.

  • Vitamin C – Deficiency causes scurvy, not neural tube defects.
